name: Chitradurga
headline: 49 child marriages carried out in six months of 2024, driven by landless poverty.
summary: Chitradurga recorded 102 child-marriage complaints between April and September 2024; 49 marriages were carried out and 53 prevented. Police point to poverty among landless families, who use early marriage to ease household burdens.

reasons.detail: 102 complaints in April-September 2024, of which 49 marriages were carried out, removing girls from school.
Police say landless families treat child marriage as an economic coping mechanism.

reasons.factor: Social customs in a tribal-dominated district
reasons.detail: In a legislative reply, social customs were blamed as one reason for dropout in two tribal-dominated districts, Chitradurga and Chamarajanagara.

The district child protection officer reported 201 child-marriage complaints from April 2024 to April 2025. A 13-year-old Class 8 girl escaped a family marriage in June 2025; a 15-year-old case in Challakere also drew child-rights group attention.

Officials credited the 2023 top SSLC rank partly to approaching and counselling parents of absent pupils, which implies absenteeism before the exam was a recognised problem. Counselling centres also addressed exam anxiety.

Challakere and Molakalmuru are described as the worst drought-hit taluks, with families leaving for Bengaluru garment, construction and security work. The reports do not directly measure effects on children's schooling.
The 2025 pass rate fell to 63.21 percent, 23rd in the state, so a larger share of candidates faced failure. No source here links this to Chitradurga dropout directly.

responses.text: Gram panchayats that prevent child marriage get a Rs 50,000 reward.
Schools approached and counselled parents of absent SSLC pupils, ran morning and evening classes and set up exam-anxiety counselling centres in Hosadurga block (2023).
Police and the Child Welfare Committee rescued the Class 8 girl in June 2025 and placed her at a Bala Mandir care centre.
